issues.legal_issue: A High Court may set aside a factual finding in a second appeal when the finding is perverse because it rests on misread evidence and lacks evidentiary support.
material_facts: The lower appellate court found that a one-year agricultural lease had continued for a further year.
The High Court found that the lower appellate court had misread the evidence in reaching that conclusion.
The Supreme Court found no evidence that possession continued under a renewed or extended lease after the original lease expired.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in setting aside the lower appellate court’s finding as perverse.
issues.legal_principle: The High Court’s interference was justified not merely because it might have assessed the evidence differently, but because the lower appellate court misread the evidence, leading to a perverse conclusion and miscarriage of justice. The judgment cites no specific provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

rule.if: second_appeal_from_decree and lower_appellate_found_lease_continued and (evidence_was_misread or no_evidence_supported_continuation)

predicates.second_appeal_from_decree: A party brought a second appeal from a decree entered after a lower appellate court decided the case.
predicates.lower_appellate_found_lease_continued: The lower appellate court found that a lease continued beyond its original term.
predicates.evidence_was_misread: The High Court found that the lower appellate court misread the evidence when making that finding.
predicates.no_evidence_supported_continuation: The record contained no evidence supporting continuation of the lease beyond its original term.

issues.definition: When a second appeal concerns a lower appellate finding that a lease continued, and the evidence was misread or does not support continuation, the High Court may set aside that perverse finding.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court has jurisdiction over a possession suit based on title when the revenue-law exclusions concern specified revenue matters and do not exclude civil determination of title.
material_facts: The purchaser of agricultural land brought a civil suit for possession based on title.
The former lessee pursued revenue proceedings seeking recognition of Bhumiswami rights.
The relevant revenue remedies concerned restoration of possession and conferral of statutory rights, while the determination of title was not within the revenue authority’s jurisdiction.
The trial court decided that the civil court had jurisdiction, and that finding was not challenged in the subsequent appeals.
issues.conclusion: The civil court had jurisdiction to try the suit for possession based on title.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 250 and 257 of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code provide for specified revenue remedies and exclude civil jurisdiction for specified matters, including decisions concerning reinstatement under Section 250 and claims concerning statutory rights under Section 190. Those provisions do not make the revenue authority the forum for determining title. The Court relied on the Madhya Pradesh High Court Full Bench decision in Ramgopal v. Chetu [1976 RN 146], which held that determination of title is the province of the civil court and that its jurisdiction cannot be excluded by implication absent an express provision to the contrary; it also noted consistent decisions of that High Court.

predicates.title_based_possession_suit: A claimant brought a civil suit seeking possession of land on the basis of title.
predicates.revenue_authority_lacks_title_determinat: The revenue authority’s assigned functions do not include determining the title asserted in the civil suit.
predicates.revenue_code_excludes_only_specified_rev: The applicable revenue law excludes civil jurisdiction for specified revenue matters without expressly excluding civil determination of title.

issues.definition: When a possession suit rests on title, the revenue authority cannot determine that title, and the revenue-law exclusions cover only specified matters, the civil court may try the suit.
